title: Reading Data with ADO.NET
description: Learn to read data using SqlDataReader in connected mode and SqlDataAdapter with DataTable in disconnected mode.

data.text: Reading data is the most common database operation. ADO.NET provides two primary approaches: the **connected** approach using `SqlDataReader`, and the **disconnected** approach using `SqlDataAdapter` and `DataTable`. Each has distinct trade-offs.

Every ADO.NET operation starts with a **SqlConnection**. It represents a physical session with the SQL Server database. You must open the connection before executing commands and close it afterward to release resources back to the connection pool.

data.title: Creating and Opening a SqlConnection
data.content: Always wrap the connection in a using statement so it is disposed automatically.

data.title: Connection pooling
data.text: SqlConnection uses connection pooling by default. Calling Close() or disposing the connection returns it to the pool rather than truly closing the physical connection. This makes ADO.NET very efficient for repeated operations.

**SqlDataReader** provides a forward-only, read-only stream of rows from the database. It is the most efficient way to read large result sets because it processes one row at a time without loading the entire result set into memory.

data.caption: Data flow using SqlDataReader in connected mode
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant App as Application
    participant Conn as SqlConnection
    participant Cmd as SqlCommand
    participant Reader as SqlDataReader
    participant DB as Database
    App->>Conn: new SqlConnection(connectionString)
    App->>Conn: Open()
    Conn->>DB: Establish session
    App->>Cmd: new SqlCommand(query, connection)
    App->>Cmd: ExecuteReader()
    Cmd->>DB: Send SQL query
    DB-->>Reader: Return result set
    loop For each row
        App->>Reader: Read()
        Reader-->>App: Next row
        App->>Reader: Get value by column name
    end
    App->>Reader: Dispose (implicit via using)
    App->>Conn: Close()

items: The connection must be **open** before calling ExecuteReader().
Only one SqlDataReader can be active per connection at a time (unless MARS is enabled).
The Read() method advances to the next row and returns false when there are no more rows.
Access column values using the column name (string) or ordinal index (int).
Use GetOrdinal() once to map column names to indexes for better performance.

data.text: Hard-coding column names is error-prone. If the database schema changes, your code breaks silently. Use `FieldCount`, `GetName()`, and `GetValue()` to iterate columns dynamically.

data.title: Dynamic Column Reading
data.content: Iterate over all columns without hard-coding names.

data.text: You can return multiple result sets from a single query by separating them with a semicolon. Use `NextResult()` to advance the reader to the next result set.

data.title: Reading Multiple Result Sets
data.content: Query two tables in one round-trip.

data.text: **SqlDataAdapter** fills a **DataTable** with data from the database. Unlike SqlDataReader, it opens and closes the connection automatically, so you can work with the data after the connection is closed.
The DataTable is an in-memory representation of a database table. You can filter, sort, and modify rows locally, then use the DataAdapter to push changes back to the database.

data.text: Using a Stored Procedure with DataAdapter
You can also use a stored procedure instead of raw SQL. Set the `CommandType` to `CommandType.StoredProcedure`.

cards.title: SqlDataReader
cards.description: Forward-only, read-only stream of data. Requires an open connection.

cards.title: SqlDataAdapter + DataTable
cards.description: Fills an in-memory DataTable and closes the connection automatically.

data.title: Exercise: Read Inventory Data
data.description: Write code that reads all Inventory records using both approaches.
steps: Create a controller action that uses SqlDataReader to read all Inventory rows.
Map each row to an Inventory model object and add it to a list.
Return the list to a view and display the data in a simple HTML table.
Repeat the same action using SqlDataAdapter and DataTable.
Compare the code structure and note the differences.
data.expectedOutcome: You can read data from SQL Server using both connected and disconnected patterns and understand when to choose each.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: SqlDataReader is the fastest way to read data but requires an open connection.
SqlDataAdapter automatically manages the connection and fills a DataTable.
Use NextResult() to read multiple result sets from a single query.
Disconnected mode is better when you need to work with data offline.
data.takeaway: Next, you will use these reading skills to build complete Create, Read, Update, and Delete operations.
